title: MSA/DPA Redline Decomposition: Modular Liability Clauses, Auto-Estimate, and Escalation SLAs
creator: Anika Shah
description: Problem: Enterprise sales are slowed by lengthy MSA/DPA negotiation cycles driven by liability and indemnity redlines. Current legal review is manual and binary (approve/deny), creating inconsistent outcomes and long SLAs for high-value customers. Goal: Create a modular redline approach that decomposes MSA/DPA into composable liability clause templates, a salesperson-facing auto-estimate tool that returns suggested liability caps and pricing flags based on inputs (ARR, industry, data sensitivity), and a triage/escalation SLA matrix for legal to act on. Deliverables: 1) Canonical set of modular liability clause templates (low/medium/high exposure) with recommended pricing adjustments; 2) Sales-facing auto-estimate spreadsheet + UI mock that outputs recommended cap, indemnity language, and whether auto-approve is allowed; 3) An SLA matrix for legal/escalation with clear decision steps and fallback options (escrow, third-party warranty, insurer requirement); 4) Integration plan for Contract Redline Queue in Console and telemetry to measure time-to-approve and pricing uplift.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical library of at least 6 modular liability/indemnity clause variants checked by Legal and Security

Sales auto-estimate prototype that returns a recommended liability cap and pricing delta given inputs (ARR, sector, data_classification) with at least 80% agreement rate against manual legal sample of 40 prior deals
Escalation SLA matrix documented and committed to: auto-approve < 24h, legal triage < 3 business days, senior-legal escalation < 7 business days
Telemetry hooks defined for instrumenting decision outcomes, time-to-first-response, and pricing delta capture in the Contract Queue
Implementation plan with dependencies and engineering scope for Console integration accepted by Eng and Legal
